correctness.rationale: The chosen one-parameter subgroup gives pairwise distinct weights to every coordinate tensor by uniqueness of binary expansion, hence the ambient dual fixed locus is exactly the coordinate set. For any coordinate functional, two positive-dimensional factors provide nonzero kernel vectors; the multilinear tangent formula then shows that the functional annihilates every tangent summand at the resulting Segre point, so the coordinate hyperplane lies in the projective dual. Thus the dual fixed locus contains all and only the ambient coordinate fixed points. Euler localization gives the claimed Euler characteristic, and constructible additivity gives the zero Euler characteristic of the complement. No smoothness of the projective dual is used. The checker independently verifies the finite weight-separation and tangent-point combinatorics over a broad grid.

value.rationale: Projective duals of Segre varieties are central objects in multilinear algebra, with the nondefective cases defining hyperdeterminants. The theorem gives one closed topological invariant for every higher tensor format, including dual-defective cases, and shows that the dual variety is Euler-indistinguishable from the entire ambient dual projective space. The equivalent vanishing theorem for the open set of non-tangent multilinear forms is uniform across all dimensions. This is a natural structural classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
